contributions.statement: Accept an agent's bug or defect claim only when an executable proof reproduces it (for Java, a failing test that the fix turns green), with the stage break and acceptance check enforced in code rather than described in the prompt; general agents given the same pipeline as a prompt reported 28-60% unreproducible findings.
contributions.evidence: §V-B1 Table VIII on 100 CyberGym projects: Claude Code 49% FP, Codex 60%, Sorcar 28% vs Revelio 0% (by construction, since only sanitizer-confirmed PoVs are reported; audit); §V-C Table IX prompt-vs-enforced ladder is ~10 cases (weak). C/C++ sanitizer oracle.

contributions.statement: Spend the cheap model on broad hypothesis generation and the strong model only on the executable-confirmation stage, which carries most of the cost.
contributions.evidence: §VI and App. C-A/C-B pilot sweep: Haiku 4.5 generation + Sonnet 4.6 confirmation; Stage 2 is 57.84% of cost (App. D). Configuration chosen on a 10-case pilot that may overlap the evaluation (audit); Revelio uses the most tokens per vulnerability.

reason: Measured evidence that a prompt-described verify step leaves high false-positive rates while a code-enforced executable oracle removes them; the domain differs, but the gate pattern transfers.
